text.tspan: Everyday English - C1 - 2026/09/15 - 01 - Essay
People share a meal and conversation.
Pexels · 9220890
Around the table
The decision to share a meal may appear ordinary, yet it exposes a recurring tension between arrangements that make life
manageable and experiences that resist being prescribed. A defensible approach combines proportionate preparation with a
willingness to reconsider whose interests a plan serves.
Preparation has value because a simple plan leaves time for conversation. In the present case, we prepare the vegetables before our
guests arrive. Such an intervention is modest, but that modesty is its strength: it removes a foreseeable obstacle without claiming to
determine the entire experience. Structure is useful to the extent that it releases attention rather than consuming it.
That argument requires a qualification, however: sharing the work helps everyone feel included. For instance, each guest brings one
dish and helps clear the table. An arrangement that appears efficient from one standpoint may impose costs elsewhere. Listening to
those affected is therefore not an optional gesture of goodwill; it supplies information without which the plan cannot be adequately
evaluated.
The resulting principle is one of proportion. Preparation deserves support when it clarifies responsibilities and protects time, while
responsiveness prevents it from hardening into an end in itself. To judge the experience well is to examine both what the arrangement
enables and what it may inadvertently exclude.
BUILD YOUR OWN · State a focused main idea. Develop one supporting reason in each body paragraph, with a concrete example.
Conclude by connecting the two reasons without introducing a new argument. Use the structure as a model; write about an
experience of your own.
Apply the idea to a real situation, then answer: What two reasons support the main idea? Explain one example.
